source.authors: Lanfang Sun, Emi Kawano-Yamashita, Takashi Nagata, Hisao Tsukamoto, Yuji Furutani, Mitsumasa Koyanagi, Akihisa Terakita
source.title: Distribution of Mammalian-Like Melanopsin in Cyclostome Retinas Exhibiting a Different Extent of Visual Functions

where: Results, Spectroscopic characterization and photosensitivity of the melanopsins
method: absorption spectrum of recombinant lamprey melanopsin expressed in COS-1 cells, reconstituted with 11-cis retinal, purified on 1D4-agarose, recorded at 10 C with a Shimadzu UV-2450; value given as approximate
conditions: Not a native retinal measurement: the melanopsin cDNA of the river lamprey (animals supplied by a university colleague; the paper does not say whether they were wild-caught) was expressed in cultured COS-1 cells, the protein reconstituted with 11-cis retinal, detergent-extracted and purified, and its dark-state spectrum recorded at 10 C. The paper gives no replicate count for the spectrum and no fit statistic, and states the value as 'approximately'. The Abstract does not give the number (it says only that the recombinant pigment is blue light-sensitive). A hagfish (Eptatretus burgeri) melanopsin could not be purified, so no hagfish spectrum is reported. The paper reports no photoreceptor (rod or cone) lambda max and no behavioural light response; Ca2+ imaging with 500 ms blue light (12 cells, Fig 2 legend) is a separate result not filed.
quote: The absorption maximum of the lamprey melanopsin was approximately 480 nm …
note: Sentence cut after the value; cut text begins with the figure reference '(Fig. 2A)' and continues ', indicating that it is a blue light-sensitive pigment...' (tail read in audit 338: ', indicating that it is a blue light-sensitive pigment and has spectroscopic properties that are similar to the mammalian ones', then citations; the authors' interpretation, not a qualifier of the value). The cut drops no qualifier of the 480 nm; 'approximately' kept. Start of the sentence confirmed by a second pass (first words 'The absorption maximum of the lamprey melanopsin was'; the preceding sentence ends 'were unable to obtain a purified hagfish melanopsin'). New trait for this species (no Lethenteron or DOI hit anywhere in docs/ or in desk-d23*/d24* evidence). Family and order as filed on main for Petromyzontidae (Petromyzontiformes); the name Lethenteron camtschaticum is not in gbif-names.tsv, WoRMS not opened (refused per rules); OBIS (audit 338): Lethenteron camtschaticum (Tilesius, 1811), accepted, Petromyzontidae, Petromyzontiformes, taxonID 101173, and Lethenteron japonicum (Martens, 1868) unaccepted with accepted name L. camtschaticum (taxonID 298380); the paper uses L. japonicum only in a reference title. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 with content-version unspecified (accepted pairing). Crossref authors (7), volume 9, issue 9 and year 2014 agree with the page.

source.authors: Leo Peichl, Sonja Meimann, Irina Solovei, Irene L. Gügel, Christina Geiger, Nicole Schauerte, Karolina Goździewska-Harłajczuk, Joanna E. Klećkowska-Nawrot, Gudrun Wibbelt, Silke Haverkamp
source.title: Eye features and retinal photoreceptors of the nocturnal aardvark (Orycteropus afer, Tubulidentata)

method: external eye dimensions of one fixed eye (aardvark 1); approximate value; the text adds that the axial length is probably an underestimate because the cornea had collapsed (the eye, punctured for fixative penetration, lost some vitreous and aqueous humour, with a collapse of the cornea and a slight deformation of the eyeball during fixation)
conditions: Two zoo aardvarks that had died of natural causes: aardvark 1, a nearly 25-year-old male from Frankfurt Zoo that died of old age, whose right eye was removed one day post mortem and immersion-fixed in 4% formalin for 24 h at 4 C; aardvark 2, a nearly 6-year-old female from Wrocław Zoo that died of perinatal complications, whose eyes were enucleated immediately after death and fixed in buffered formaldehyde (a third animal was used only for serum thyroid hormone). Most findings in the paper come from aardvark 1. External eye dimensions were recorded after fixation. n = 1 eye for the axial length; the paper gives no mean or range for the species.
quote: The eye of aardvark 1 had an equatorial diameter of approx. 23.0 mm and an axial length of approx. 21.2 mm.
note: Whole Results sentence (20 words), read in full in one piece. Value is the single eye's 'approx.' axial length, measured after fixation in a 25-year-old captive male; the paper states the figure is likely an underestimate (collapsed cornea), which is a qualifier in a neighbouring sentence and is given here. Not a species mean. New trait for this species: eye_axial_length_mm is a key already on main (e.g. Molothrus ater, Hippopotamus amphibius) though absent from the checker list. Family Orycteropodidae confirmed by the Mammal Diversity Database (family page lists the single species Orycteropus afer; order page lists Tubulidentata > Orycteropodidae; audit 338); the paper prints no family name; order Tubulidentata as printed in the paper; name Orycteropus afer accepted (GBIF species page returned by search). No Orycteropus or this DOI anywhere in docs/ or desk-d23*/d24* evidence. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Crossref authors (10), volume 20, issue 3, year 2025 agree.

value: reflective tapetum lucidum with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum; retinal pigment epithelium in front of it unpigmented

source.authors: Leo Peichl, Sonja Meimann, Irina Solovei, Irene L. Gügel, Christina Geiger, Nicole Schauerte, Karolina Goździewska-Harłajczuk, Joanna E. Klećkowska-Nawrot, Gudrun Wibbelt, Silke Haverkamp
source.title: Eye features and retinal photoreceptors of the nocturnal aardvark (Orycteropus afer, Tubulidentata)

method: gross inspection of the opened fixed eyecup (a bright yellowish fundus band from temporal to nasal periphery), histology and transmission electron microscopy of fixed eyes of two zoo aardvarks; Figure 4 (choroid and tapetum) is labelled aardvark 1; the tapetum fibrosum reading rests on TEM fibrils with the cross-striation of native collagen
conditions: Two zoo aardvarks that had died of natural causes: aardvark 1, a nearly 25-year-old male from Frankfurt Zoo that died of old age, whose right eye was removed one day post mortem and immersion-fixed in 4% formalin for 24 h at 4 C; aardvark 2, a nearly 6-year-old female from Wrocław Zoo that died of perinatal complications, whose eyes were enucleated immediately after death and fixed in buffered formaldehyde (a third animal was used only for serum thyroid hormone). Most findings in the paper come from aardvark 1. The paper states 'in contrast to some previous studies' (earlier reports had denied a tapetum). The Results sentence 'This bright band had the appearance of a tapetum lucidum, its dorso-ventral width was larger in the temporal than the nasal...' was read to 125 characters only. The paper does not say which animal each histological statement rests on beyond the Figure 4 caption, nor whether a tapetum was seen in aardvark 2. The authors state that their fixation was not optimized for electron microscopy, so the substructure of the tapetal fibrils may be an artefact, and that their material did not allow them to determine whether the fibril domains are intracellular (suggesting a tapetum cellulosum) or extracellular (suggesting a tapetum fibrosum). Earlier studies are split: Franz, Matas et al. and Freeman et al. describe no tapetum in the aardvark eye, while Walls and Paszta et al. describe one.
quote: In contrast to some previous studies, we found that the aardvark eye has a reflective tapetum lucidum with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum, in front of which the retinal pigment epithelium is unpigmented.
note: Whole Abstract sentence (33 words) read verbatim in two abutting pieces in one response ('...reflective tapetum lucidum' | 'with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum, in front of ... unpigmented.') and joined identically on a second pass. Value is the sentence's own claim, a presence finding. Same source, licence and Crossref check as the axial-length record; not on main for this species.

source.authors: Fanny de Busserolles, John L. Fitzpatrick, N. Justin Marshall, Shaun P. Collin
source.title: The Influence of Photoreceptor Size and Distribution on Optical Sensitivity in the Eyes of Lanternfishes (Myctophidae)

method: retinal wholemounts, optical fractionator stereology (rods counted at x100 oil, about 200 sites per retina), topographic maps of three individuals
conditions: Wild-caught mesopelagic lanternfish; per the Methods, samples came from several research cruises in the Coral Sea (RV Cape Ferguson), from the Peru-Chile trench (FS Sonne) and from collaborators in Western Australia, the Western Mediterranean and the Bay of Biscay, and the text read does not say which source supplied the B. longipes specimens (Table S1 not read); the paper does not give trawl type, capture depth per specimen, or life stage. Three individuals of B. longipes were mapped (Figure 3 caption: 'three different individuals of Bolinichthys longipes'; sizes are in Table 2 and Table S1, not read). Eyes fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde or Karnovsky's fixative; the authors state fixation quality 'was often outside of our control' (delay in preserving specimens on deck, capture depth). Retinas flattened by radial cuts and counted by the optical fractionator, one to three individuals per species across the five wholemount species. The value is the range of the peak density across the three individuals, not a mean; the authors attribute intraspecific differences in peak density mainly to the size of the individuals examined, larger individuals having higher densities across the retina and more rods per retina, so the range reflects specimen size (sizes in Table 2 and Table S1, not read); the paper does not mention tissue shrinkage, measured or corrected; central-retina densities from wholemounts and sections agreed within 4-10% except in Lampanyctus parvicauda, where sections underestimated rod density by about 30%. The same Results section also gives a lower peak for Diaphus brachycephalus (418 x10^3 rods/mm2) and a streak in Myctophum brachygnathum (1840 to 2280 x10^3, three individuals); neither is filed here. The text attributes an 89 um maximum rod outer segment length to B. supralateralis in Results and to B. longipes in Discussion; that inconsistency is not filed.
quote: In B. longipes, the arch specialisation is present spanning the dorsal-temporal-ventral part of the retina with a peak density of rod photoreceptor cells situated in temporal retina with densities ranging from 650 to 760×103 rods mm−2 …
note: Whole Results sentence read verbatim in four abutting pieces in one response, each piece under 120 characters and numbered by the page tool ('In B. longipes ... of the retina' | 'with a peak density of rod photoreceptor cells situated in temporal retina' | 'with densities ranging from 650 to 760×103 rods mm−2' | '([Table 2]).'), so the end was seen; the trailing table reference '(Table 2).' is cut and marked; the exponent is printed as '×103' (10^3) in the text. New trait for this species: rod_density_mm2 is a key already on main (rabbit rows) though absent from the checker list. Family and order as filed on main for Myctophidae (Myctophiformes); the paper names the family in the Introduction. Species name as printed; WoRMS not opened (refused per rules); OBIS (audit 338): Bolinichthys longipes (Brauer, 1906), accepted, Myctophidae, Myctophiformes, taxonID 272650, not in gbif-names.tsv. No Bolinichthys, Myctophum or this DOI in docs/ outside audit/ALL (an unrelated optical_sensitivity row for Lampanyctus from a book) or in desk-d23*/d24* evidence. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version unspecified (accepted pairing). Crossref authors (4), volume 9, issue 6 and year 2014 agree.
